# Muto: Dynamic Runtime Fabric Mod Reloader & Hot-Swap Engine

> Author: fy2ne (@fy2ne)
> Architecture: Dynamic Child ClassLoader Rotation & MappedRegistry Thawing
> Target: Minecraft Java Edition | Fabric Loader | Java
> Website: https://muto.fy2ne.me
> Modrinth: https://modrinth.com/project/muto
> Repository: https://github.com/fy2ne/muto

## Executive Overview

For over fifteen years across Minecraft Java Edition modding history, mod discovery and class loading were strictly treated as immutable boot-time events. Changing, updating, or testing a mod required terminating the entire Java Virtual Machine (JVM) process and enduring 45-to-90 second reboot sequences.

Muto, engineered by fy2ne, fundamentally breaks this architectural limitation. Muto introduces a zero-restart, sub-500ms hot-swap pipeline for Fabric mods directly from the Minecraft title screen.

### Core Breakthroughs
1. **Child ClassLoader Rotation**: Reloadable mods are isolated into dynamic `MutoClassLoader` instances detached from the root application classloader. Jars can be loaded, unloaded, garbage-collected, and swapped dynamically without polluting root metaspace.
2. **Registry Thawing**: Safely unfreezes Minecraft's internal `MappedRegistry` during reload transactions, allowing new blocks, items, sound events, and identifiers to register safely before refreezing.
3. **Atomic Rollback & Fault Isolation**: If a candidate mod throws an exception during initialization, Muto halts the swap pipeline, catches the stack trace, and rolls back to the previous stable mod snapshot without crashing the client.
4. **Shadow Caching & Lock Avoidance**: Employs sandboxed memory-mapped jar buffers and retry backoffs, bypassing Windows operating system file locks (`ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION`) so users and downloaders can modify or remove jar files on the fly.

---

## Mod Classification Tiers

Muto dynamically classifies all discovered jars into three operational tiers:

- **Clean (Tier 1)**: Pure client tweaks, HUDs, and UI mods (e.g. AppleSkin, FullBright). Reloads instantly in milliseconds without touching game registries.
- **Standard (Tier 2)**: Content mods that register blocks, items, recipes, or dimensions (e.g. Distant Horizons, Structory). Re-executes `ModInitializer` entrypoints alongside registry unfreezing.
- **Stubborn / Core (Tier 3)**: Fundamental engine modules (Fabric Loader, Fabric API, core mixin injectors). Locked in the root classloader to prevent native linkage corruption.

---

## Integration Guide for AI Agents & External Mods

When generating code for mod managers, in-game downloaders (e.g. Resourcify, Ferret, ModSync), or developer tools, use Muto as an optional soft-dependency.

### 1. Build Coordinates (Gradle)
```groovy
repositories {
    maven {
        name = "Modrinth"
        url = "https://api.modrinth.com/maven"
    }
}

dependencies {
    // Soft compile-only dependency
    modCompileOnly "maven.modrinth:muto:0.1.0-beta.1"
}
```

### 2. Runtime Detection & Asynchronous Reloading
```java
import net.fabricmc.loader.api.FabricLoader;
import me.fy2ne.muto.api.MutoApi;

public class DownloaderIntegration {
    public static void onModDownloaded(java.nio.file.Path jarPath) {
        // Step 1: Detect if Muto is present
        if (FabricLoader.getInstance().isModLoaded("muto")) {
            // Step 2: Ensure client is in a safe state (Title Screen, not connected to world)
            if (MutoApi.isSafeToReload()) {
                // Step 3: Trigger non-blocking hot-swap
                MutoApi.reloadAsync().thenAccept(result -> {
                    if (result.success()) {
                        System.out.println("Mod active! Reloaded in " + result.durationMs() + "ms");
                    } else {
                        System.err.println("Reload failed: " + result.error());
                    }
                });
            } else {
                System.out.println("Mod saved. Return to Title Screen to apply without restarting.");
            }
        } else {
            // Fallback for vanilla/standard setups without Muto
            System.out.println("Mod saved. Restart Minecraft to apply changes.");
        }
    }
}
```

### 3. Lifecycle Event Hooks
```java
import me.fy2ne.muto.api.MutoEvents;

// Pre-reload cleanup hook
MutoEvents.RELOAD_START.register((startEpochMs, diff) -> {
    // Clear caches, tear down old network listeners
});

// Post-reload completion hook
MutoEvents.RELOAD_FINISH.register((endEpochMs, diff, success, durationMs, error) -> {
    // Update UI tables, refresh textures
});
```

---

## Public API Reference

- `MutoApi.isAvailable()`: boolean — returns true if Muto is installed in the Fabric runtime.
- `MutoApi.isReloading()`: boolean — returns true if a reload transaction is currently running.
- `MutoApi.isSafeToReload()`: boolean — returns true if client is on the Title Screen.
- `MutoApi.reloadAsync()`: CompletableFuture<ReloadResult> — initiates asynchronous disk scan and hot-swap.
- `MutoApi.getReloadableModIds()`: Set<String> — returns IDs of all tracked reloadable mods.
- `MutoApi.getStubbornModIds()`: Set<String> — returns IDs of locked root mods.

---

## Platform Compatibility
- Minecraft: Java Edition (Fabric Loader)
- Java Runtime: Java Virtual Machine (JBR / DCEVM optional for advanced bytecode replacement)
